Maladaptive Strategies.value: I dwell on what other people have done to me

Threat.value: I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment
When something takes longer than expected I assume something bad is happening
I watch other people closely for signs that they might harm me

Memory.value: When the memory returns I feel so overwhelmed by emotion that I have to stop
My memories of the frightening event are like a film that plays over and over.
Sometimes I can recall what happened but feel completely numb, as if it happened to a stranger

Negative Appraisals.value: My reactions since the event mean that I am going crazy
I was betrayed by someone I trusted
You can never know who will harm you

issues.item: Triggers: Positive Emotion Confusion: Positive emotions
issues.explanation: 'Positive emotions' as a trigger is not impossible, but in this profile it sits awkwardly with the rest of the trigger/threat pattern. The strongest formulation link is Triggers → Threat, yet the other trigger items point to direct trauma recall and general discomfort, while positive emotion confusion is a qualitatively different trigger type that is not meaningfully reflected in the threat, appraisal, or memory items.

issues.item: Threat: Noticing Weapons: I notice potential weapons or dangerous objects in any environment
issues.explanation: Hypervigilance for weapons can occur, but here it is hard to reconcile with the refugee trauma narrative as represented elsewhere in the profile. The accompanying appraisals focus on betrayal and global mistrust, and the triggers focus on event recall rather than environmental danger cues; this makes pervasive scanning for weapons feel clinically disconnected from the rest of the selected items.

issues.item: Negative Appraisals: Betrayal: I was betrayed by someone I trusted
issues.explanation: 'I was betrayed by someone I trusted' is the clearest inconsistency. For a refugee trauma profile, this appraisal could fit if the trauma centrally involved trusted-person betrayal, but nothing in the triggers, memory, threat, or strategies suggests an interpersonal betrayal-based trauma. The rest of the profile points more toward generalized danger and intrusive recall than betrayal-specific PTSD.

issues.item: Maladaptive Strategies: Avoid Work or Study: Going to work or study
issues.explanation: 'Avoid work or study' is demographically implausible for an 80-year-old married male rabbi unless there is clear context that he is still actively working or studying. Because occupation was given as rabbi, this is not impossible, but the item as phrased is substantially less coherent than the other strategies and is the most questionable item on demographic grounds.
